fact: Sierra Loaded reports the Electronic Transactions Act, enacted in January 2019 by its account, gives legal recognition to electronic signatures, consumer protection and digital communications in courts.

Sierra Loaded reports that the Act's enforcement structures, including digital certification authorities, electronic evidence procedures, dispute resolution and penalties, had not been fully established when a government dialogue on implementing it was held on 27-28 July 2026.
The SierraLII record gives the Electronic Transactions Act, Act 89 of 2019, assent and commencement on 5 December 2019, promulgation on 14 January 2020, and marks it in force.

The Government Printing Department gazetted a 26-clause Bill entitled the Electronic Transactions Act, 2018 on 24 January 2019, with commencement date blank, covering legal effect of electronic information, validity of transactions, consumer protection and service provider liability.

The UNECA digital trade profile names the Electronic Transactions Act of 2019 as a Sierra Leone framework carrying intermediary safe-harbour and consumer-protection provisions, though no general e-commerce law; the profile has no date, so its proxied publication year 2023 is used.
The embassy's account lists an Electronic Transactions Act among Sierra Leone's enacted legislation, and says it is currently under review.
